name: Hardrock Hundred Mile Endurance Run
organizer: Hardrock Hundred Mile Endurance Run (nonprofit), directed by Dale Garland
date_display: Early July (typical; exact date shifts — course direction alternates yearly)
notes: San Juan Mountains loop; ~33,000 ft climb; avg elevation 11,186 ft; summits Handies Peak (14,048 ft — highest point in any race in this dataset). One of the hardest ultras in the world to enter: lottery + trail-work requirement. Part of the Grand Slam of Ultrarunning.

name: Leadville Trail 100 Run
notes: aka 'Race Across the Sky'. Out-and-back on Colorado Trail & dirt roads; climbs Hope Pass (12,532 ft); ~15,744 ft total climb. Western States/Grand Slam qualifier; 30-hr cutoff.

name: Leadville Silver Rush 50
notes: High-altitude mining-road course above 10,000 ft. 2026 run cancelled due to Willow Fire (per The Colorado Sun, July 9, 2026). Expected to return; this entry represents a typical year.

name: San Juan Solstice 50
notes: San Juan Mountains; ~12,000 ft climb along the Continental Divide. Lottery entry (300 runners); Western States qualifier; benefits Lake City EMS.

name: Ouray 100 Mile Endurance Run
notes: San Juan Mountains; ~41,862 ft gain; historic mining routes. 2026 edition cancelled ~2 weeks before race day due to Gold Mountain wildfire. Expected to return; this entry represents a typical year.

name: Ouray 50 Mile Endurance Run
notes: San Juan Mountains. Sister event to the Ouray 100; no longer a UTMB qualifier (stopped 2022).

name: The Sneffles Round ("Sneffelupagus")
notes: ~43,000 ft climb; ~34 peaks including 14er Mt. Sneffels; ~70% off-trail; self-navigated. Free entry; applicants vetted for mountaineering/routefinding skill; ~35-runner cap; 100-hr limit.

name: San Juan Softie 100
notes: San Juan Mountains region; less technical variant of the area's high-mountain 100-milers. Featured on the curated UltraSignup Colorado list.

name: Telluride Mountain Run
companion_distances: Hill Climb & shorter options historically offered
notes: High San Juans above Telluride; above 13,000 ft; Mile-and-a-Half-of-Sky ridge; Telluride Peak (13,509 ft). Founded by Dakota Jones as a 38-miler. Exact 2026 distance lineup should be confirmed with organizer.

name: Box Canyon Trail Races
notes: Climbs from town past Bridal Veil Falls to ~13,000 ft. Ultra-adjacent event (30K is below the standard 50K threshold); grouped with Telluride-area ultra race weekends.

name: Creede 50/100
notes: San Juans; climbs above 12,000 ft; 20,000+ ft gain; Continental Divide singletrack; start/finish Basham Park. 100-runner cap; USFS permitted; self-reliant ethos. Not the same event as Creede Mountain Run (different organizer, different history).

name: Creede Mountain Run
organizer: Creede & Mineral County Chamber of Commerce
notes: Community race; distinct from the Tempest Adventures Creede 50/100 (different organizer, different history).

name: Silverton Alpine Marathon & 50K
notes: Alpine Loop; high point 12,930 ft at California Pass.

name: Pikes Peak Ultra
organizer: Mad Moose Events (founded by Justin Ricks)
notes: Foothills/mountain terrain beneath Pikes Peak; longer courses summit Mt. Rosa. Considered a more approachable Front Range ultra.

name: Valkyrie Trail Race
notes: Cheyenne Mountain State Park. Women-centered trail event.

name: Ram Party Trail Runs
notes: Rampart Reservoir / Buffalo Lodge Bicycle Resort; high point 9,500 ft. Weekend festival format.

name: Falcon 50
notes: Front Range foothills. Featured on the UltraSignup Colorado list.

name: Cheyenne Mountain Trail Races
notes: Cheyenne Mountain State Park. Distances confirmed: 50K / 25K / 10K.

name: Take 5 in the Garden
notes: Garden of the Gods area. Timed ultra-format event; specific duration not listed in source — confirm with organizer.

name: Ring the Springs
notes: Ring the Peak trail system.

name: Bobcat Trail Race
notes: Palmer Park sandstone/mesa terrain.

name: Rattler Trail Race
notes: Palmer Park.

name: Colorado Cold Rush Ultra
notes: Bear Creek Regional Park, High Drive, Gold Camp Road; ~9,000 ft. Winter conditions likely (snow/ice).

name: Stories Ultra
notes: No podium/age-group awards, per HPRS format.

name: Above the Clouds Ultra
notes: Starts/finishes at Woodland Park Middle School. ~4,137 ft gain on the 50K; ascends Lovell Gulch to Rampart Range Road, circles Rampart Reservoir; Pikes Peak views.

name: The Great Divide Ultra
notes: Mueller State Park; rolling single/doubletrack; 9,000+ ft elevation. First 100-miler on the CO calendar each year; non-technical; features a night 'Dark Divide' run. Three start-time variants per distance.

name: 24 Hours of Palmer Lake
notes: 0.82-mi loop at 7,240 ft.

name: Greenland Trail Races
notes: Greenland Open Space (near Larkspur). 2026 RRCA National 50K Championship; billed as 'Colorado's fastest 50K'.

name: The Bear Chase
notes: Bear Creek Lake Park, Lakewood. 100K added 2013; beginner-friendly; benefits Lakewood open space.

name: Chase the Moon 12 Hour Endurance Run
notes: Overnight 7 PM–7 AM run under the full moon. Offers a standard 50K option alongside the timed formats.

name: Barr Lake Trail Race
notes: Flat and fast course around Barr Lake State Park.

name: Indian Creek Trail Runs
notes: Pike National Forest foothills south of Denver.

name: North Fork Trail Race
notes: 100% soft-surface singletrack; 1996 burn-scar terrain SW of Denver (Buffalo Creek area). Proceeds support the North Fork Volunteer Fire Dept.

name: Sawmill Trail Runs
notes: Staunton State Park. Started as an informal 'Fat Ass' event in 2013; became an official race in 2017; moved to Staunton in 2021.

name: Golden Gate Dirty 30
notes: Golden Gate Canyon State Park. Official site (dirty30.org) states: 'Dirty 30 is permanently Cancelled.'

name: Quad Rock 50/25
notes: Lory State Park & Horsetooth Mountain Open Space. Anchor race of the 'Gnar Slam'.

name: Never Summer 100K & 60K
notes: Never Summer Mountains / Medicine Bow Mountains border; near RMNP; ~14,500 ft gain; high point North Diamond Peak (11,852 ft). Western States qualifier for 100K finishers under 23 hrs; sells out yearly.

name: Colorado 24 Hour Run
notes: Flat one-mile loop.

name: Weld Your Mettle Running Festival
notes: Plains terrain (not mountain). Virtual option available.

name: NoCo Urban Ultra & Relay
notes: Urban Greeley course. Solo or relay options for both distances.

name: Rocky's Backyard Ultra
notes: Trails bordering Rocky Mountain National Park, at the YMCA of the Rockies; ~500 ft gain per loop. $1,000 cash prize + buckles for 100-mile finishers.

name: Estes Park's Backyard Ultra
notes: Lake Estes paved loop.

name: Samson's Revenge Trail Race
notes: Estes Park / RMNP-area foothills.

name: Estes Epic Ultra Run & MTB Race
notes: Combined running + MTB weekend event.

name: Run Rabbit Run
organizer: Independent (founded/directed by Fred Abramowitz & Paul Sachs)
notes: Routt National Forest; ~22,000 ft gain (100 mi) / ~9,000 ft (50 mi). 'Hares vs. Tortoises' staggered-start format. $100,000+ overall purse, $20,000 to each 100-mile winner — largest payout of any US ultra. ~$600,000 donated to charity.

name: Continental Divide Trail Run
notes: Steamboat Ski Area base; Continental Divide; Mt. Werner area.

name: Crested Butte Ultra
notes: Gunnison National Forest singletrack. Fall-foliage timing.

name: The Grand Traverse (Mountain Run)
notes: Point-to-point across the Elk Mountains. Companion event to the winter Grand Traverse ski race.

name: Sage Burner Trail Races
organizer: Mad Moose Events (formerly One Love Endurance)
notes: Hartman Rocks high-desert sagebrush terrain (near Gunnison). A contrast to CO's typical alpine ultras.

name: Grand Mesa Ultras
notes: World's largest flat-topped mountain; alpine lakes; 10,000+ ft. Cash prizes for top 3 M/F; on-mountain camping.

name: Powderhorn Mountain Ultra & Vert Challenge
notes: Powderhorn Resort (on the Grand Mesa).

name: Kessel Run Ultra
notes: Desert terrain near Colorado National Monument; Zippity-Do-Da singletrack. Camping available on-site.

name: Aspen Backcountry
notes: Out-and-back to McNamara Hut; Elk Mountains backcountry singletrack above 10,000 ft. CORSAR card required.

name: Devil on the Divide
notes: Exceeds 13,000 ft; 6,500+ ft climb; 80% of course above 10,000 ft. Requires prior ultra experience for the 50K.

name: Snow Mountain Ranch Trail Running Festival
notes: Snow Mountain Ranch YMCA property.

name: Summits Trail Runs
notes: Granby Ranch. Confirmed distances: 50K, Marathon, Half Marathon, 6 mi, plus a 14-hr timed 'Elevation Challenge' option.

name: West Line Winder
notes: ~4,000 ft climb near the Collegiate Peaks.

name: Collegiate Peaks Trail Run
notes: Long-running local race in the Collegiate Peaks area near Buena Vista. Specific 2027 date unconfirmed.

name: TransRockies Run: Pass to Pub
notes: 3-day stage race from Leadville to Red Cliff; crosses Hope Pass and the Continental Divide. Replaced the discontinued multi-day TransRockies Run format. Capped at 500 runners.

name: High Lonesome 100
notes: Sawatch Range; Collegiate Peaks region; five alpine passes; 13,150 ft high point. Two-pool lottery; trail-work requirement; Western States qualifier; competitive/elite field.

name: Silverheels Trail Runs
notes: Avg elevation over 10,000 ft. May correspond to what some aggregators list as 'Fairplay 100M/100K' — both refer to this HPRS event in Como/Park County.

name: Sheep Mountain Trail Runs
notes: 300-runner cap; 50K distance added 2018.

name: Sangre de Cristo Trail Festival
notes: Rainbow Trail beneath the Sangre de Cristo peaks. Widest distance range of any CO ultra event: 50K through 200 mi.

name: WILD Wahatoya Runs
notes: Views of the Spanish Peaks.

name: Bridge Burner Ultra
notes: Royal Gorge Mountain Park. The 35-mi loop crosses the Royal Gorge Bridge.

name: Royal Gorge Groove
notes: Royal Gorge area.

name: Beulah Challenge and OverIt Series
notes: Beulah Valley. 32 miles (just above the 50K threshold).

name: American Heroes Run
notes: 1.05-mi loop. Timed event; '100 mi' option is a goal distance within the timed format, not a fixed-distance race.

name: Raising the Barr
notes: Lakeside loop course; solo and relay options.

name: Sourdough Snowshoe Race
notes: Roosevelt National Forest backcountry; ~10,000 ft. Donation-based winter/snowshoe event. Could not be independently confirmed as a currently active event — verify directly with Trail Trash Adventures.
